concepts.title: Crop Classification by Season
concepts.definition: Crops are categorized into two primary groups based on the specific climatic conditions and seasons in which they are cultivated.
concepts.key_idea: Agricultural timing depends on seasonal patterns like rainfall and temperature.
question_patterns: what are the two broad cropping patterns in India
distinguish between kharif and rabi crops
identify the season for sowing paddy
name two examples of rabi crops

solution_steps.explain: Check if the crop is sown in rainy season (Kharif) or winter season (Rabi).

concepts.title: Irrigation Efficiency
concepts.definition: The systematic delivery of water to crops at necessary intervals to support growth, germination, and nutrient transport.
concepts.key_idea: Water is essential for plant development and nutrient absorption.
question_patterns: calculate total water required for a field
find the volume of water needed for irrigation
determine water usage for a specific area
how much water is needed if depth is fixed

solution_steps.explain: Total water volume is the product of field area and required depth.

concepts.title: Harvest Yield Estimation
concepts.definition: The measurement of the total quantity of grain produced per unit of land area after the crop matures.
concepts.key_idea: Yield depends on land size and productivity per unit.
question_patterns: find the total production from a farm
compute the yield for a given land area
how much grain is produced in total
determine the output of the field

solution_steps.explain: Total production is calculated by multiplying the land area by the yield per acre.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A farmer grows wheat on {area} acres with a yield of {yield_per_acre} quintals per acre. Calculate the total yield.

solution_template.explain: Multiply area by yield per acre.

worked_examples.question_pattern: If a field of {area} acres produces {yield_per_acre} quintals per acre, what is the total harvest?

solution_template.explain: Multiply area by yield per acre.
